defects: Final 3-4 s is close to static: per-second change falls to 2.7-12 after the lockup. That is dead air, not a held beat.

The CMYK misregistration is the same RGB-split fringe on every glyph, including the small type in the lockup. At 1:1 it reads as a chromatic-aberration filter, not real plate offset, and it softens the edges of the copy.
In the stripe shot the large black 'Offset' collides with the 'OFFSET' rows and is unreadable. It reads as clutter, not as layering.
The repeated 'OFFSET' marquee rows are a stock kinetic-type move. They slide at constant speed, rows alternate direction, and there is no easing or staggered hand-off.
The pairs show the layered-plate frame barely changing in 1/6 s, while the colour plates drift with little visible ease or overshoot. Weight is missing from the snap into register.
Two shots run long (median 4.8 s, longest 5.9 s) with no reveal inside them strong enough to justify the hold.
The palette goes past restraint: blue, cream, cyan, magenta, yellow and black all compete in the stripe section, so there is no single accent.
gaps: Choreography: misregistration snapping into register is the right idea, but it plays as one drift and one snap. Top work would stage it as a sequence: plates arriving with different timing, overshoot and a settle, a decisive hit at the moment of registration, and the type system then building out from that hit. Right now there is a constant-speed marquee and a long static tail.

Finish: the offset should look like printing. Top work would show plate-specific ink overprint and multiply, paper texture moving under the ink, and halftone or trapping detail at 1:1, so the 'offset' is a material and not a uniform RGB-split post effect on every element.

Sound and arc: the riser into the drop at about 6 s lands well. After that, dense evenly spaced transients flatten the dynamics, and the release at 12-14 s has no strong closing hit paired with the final registration. Top work would leave more space, give the drop a designed sound for registration snapping in, and finish with a cleaner single resolve.
